thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: high - gpu-host-hang detected on gpu-rack9-node17. Impact: inference service 'rv-infer-prod' experiencing timeouts. Pager: https://pagerduty.example/INC12345

pagerduty: Triggered by check: node-heartbeat-missed (3 mins). Details: socket timeout to nvidia driver reported; node not responding to kubelet health checks.

Maya Rao: acked. I'm on it. Paging SRE lead.

Devon Patel: grabbing logs now. which zone?

Maya Rao: rack9 / us-west-2a. several pods on that node in CrashLoopBackOff or Evicted. Customer-facing routes still up but ~20% 5xx spike on gen endpoint.

Alex Chen: I see node shows NotReady in cluster: `kubectl get nodes | grep node17` returned NotReady  5m. Kubelet last log: OOM kill of kubelet process then watchdog restart.

Devon Patel: pulling dmesg from node via bastion:
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: GPU 0: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x33:0x79:971)
[ 12345.678903] NVRM: GPU at 00000000:25:00.0 has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.678905] kernel: nvidia: GPU lockup - resetting
[ 12346.000000] kernel: kernel: watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#3 stuck for 22s
```

Sasha (SRE Lead): ok this looks like a driver hang leading to kubelet instability. Plan: cordon node17, drain as best-effort, move critical pods to other racks, and fallback inference traffic to dedicated pool for high-SLA customers.

Maya Rao: cordoning node now. `kubectl cordon gpu-rack9-node17` -> succeeded. Starting drain (graceful) for non-critical pods.

Devon Patel: attempted `kubectl drain` but many pods stuck terminating due to device-plugin timeouts. Will force evict after grace window 60s.

Alex Chen: increasing replica counts on rv-infer-prod to compensate and scaling up dedicated pool by +2 gpus in us-west-2 to handle burst. Notifying deployments to avoid throttling.

pagerduty: Escalation: no ack from SRE manager within 5m, paging oncall-manager.

Maya Rao: noted. I'm taking on-call lead until handoff. Devon, can you collect the driver logs and create a minimal repro? Might be a recent driver push.

Devon Patel: grabbing /var/log/nvidia-installer.log and modprobe output. Also seeing nv_peer_mem errors. Saving tarball to s3://redwood-ops/incident/INC12345/node17-logs.tar.gz

Maya Rao: customer impact update: 4 customers on Dedicated SLO saw degraded latency; we auto-failed them to fallback model hosted on CPU with slightly higher latency but preserved throughput. Notifying CSMs.

Sasha (SRE Lead): good mitigation. Next steps: coordinate host reboot, check kernel/drivers, possibly roll back nvidia driver to previous known-good. If host recovers, validate with synthetic load and then uncordon.

Alex Chen: scheduling a rolling reboot now via metal-api. Reboot queued: job-4821. ETA 3m.

incident-bot: Reboot job started for gpu-rack9-node17 (job-4821). Monitoring boot logs.

Devon Patel: after reboot we should run `nvidia-smi -q` and a mini-inference to warm KV caches. Also check for ECC/memory errors.

Maya Rao: reboot finished. Node came back to network, but kubelet stuck in CrashLoop on start. `journalctl -u kubelet -n 200` shows repeated device plugin timeouts and then kubelet exits with OOM.

Devon Patel: guessing kernel modules allocating large pinned pages at boot. increasing kubelet cgroup limits temporarily to test.

Alex Chen: while we test, keeping node cordoned. Routing still off to this rack. Have we informed account teams?

Maya Rao: yes, accounts + CSM pinged with mitigations. Posting incident note in #customer-impact.

Sasha (SRE Lead): if node doesn't stabilize in 30m, we'll decommission and replace hardware. Start a change request with hardware team.

Devon Patel: found that nvidia-driver-520.61 was installed during last maintenance window. Rolling back to 510.47 on a test host reproduced boot success. Preparing rollback playbook for node17.

Maya Rao: go ahead with rollback on this node. Make sure to mark maintenance window and update PagerDuty with expected 45m to restore.

incident-bot: Action recorded: driver-rollback planned by Devon. ETA 45m. PagerDuty updated: INC12345 -> status: in progress.

Alex Chen: applying driver-rollback now via salt. Monitoring.

Devon Patel: rollback completed, rebooting. Reboot job-4821b started.

Maya Rao: post-rollback boot looks cleaner. `nvidia-smi` shows GPUs healthy. Kubelet came up and node registered Ready.

Devon Patel: running synthetic inference test: 1000 requests over 30s, p95 latency within SLO. No OOMs.

Sasha (SRE Lead): great. Uncordon when you're satisfied. Remember to annotate node with incident tag and create follow-up ticket to validate fleet driver versions and add preflight checks.

Maya Rao: uncordoning node17 now. `kubectl uncordon gpu-rack9-node17` -> succeeded. Pods are being scheduled.

Alex Chen: traffic gradually shifted back over 10m. Metrics show 5xx spike resolved. I'll scale down dedicated pool to normal.

Maya Rao: incident summary: root cause - problematic nvidia driver (520.61) causing GPU hangs and kernel watchdogs -> kubelet instability -> node NotReady. Mitigation - cordon/drain, scale up fallback capacity, rollback driver to 510.47, reboot, validate, uncordon. Customer impact - transient latency/5xx spike for a subset of customers; fallback prevented outages.

Sasha (SRE Lead): create postmortem ticket (PM-INC12345) and include repro steps, driver rollout gating, and automated health checks to detect early driver hangs.

Maya Rao: handing off to next oncall in 30m. If anything regresses ping me directly.

Devon Patel: logs and actions bundled in s3://redwood-ops/incident/INC12345/ and PRD runbook updated.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: INC12345 -> resolved (auto) at 1818460321.

Maya Rao: closing thread. :white_check_mark:
